title: Kernel fallback probing and KV eviction safety playbook
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook captures the proposed safety net for introducing kernel-level fallback probing (fast-path -> safe-path) together with KV-cache eviction guardrails during speculative decoding on production clusters. It combines acceptance criteria, rollback triggers, observability signals, and short experiment notes. Goal: enable an incremental rollout of a hybrid kernel routing + KV eviction policy without exposing downstream apps to correctness regressions or unacceptable latency/cost regressions.

Background / motivation
- We're introducing a fast, lower-precision kernel variant (FP-fast) for critical prefixes to reduce token latency. FP-fast can sometimes produce outlier tokens or require a quick fallback to FP-safe (higher precision).
- Speculative decoding increases concurrency and cache pressure on the KV store. Aggressive eviction (to keep memory bounded) can break long-context workloads or lead to coherent-kv misses during handoffs between fast and safe kernels.
- Previous integration runs (see linked PR/Confluence) showed small p95 improvements but occasional spikes in output regression when the fallback path and eviction overlapped. We need a deterministic, observable rollout plan.

High-level approach
1) Probing window: for each incoming request we allow N speculative fast-token steps (config: speculative_steps), but after M fallbacks in K seconds we throttle speculative usage for that model/route.
2) KV eviction soft-limit: we maintain a soft-high watermark (cache_soft) and a hard-high watermark (cache_hard). When cache_soft is reached we begin LRU-preservation (bump TTL for recent prefixes used in speculative flows). When cache_hard is reached we gate speculative kernels and force FP-safe.
3) Fallback probing loop: on an observed mismatch (model confidence signal or validation token entropy threshold), we immediately route the next token to FP-safe, and mark the session as "fallbacked". If fallback rate > threshold over a minute, reduce speculative_steps for the route.

Config knobs (tunable)
- speculative_steps: integer (default 2)
- fallback_rate_threshold: percent (default 0.8%) measured per-1m window
- cache_soft_fraction: fraction of total mem (default 0.65)
- cache_hard_fraction: fraction of total mem (default 0.85)
- preserve_ttl_multiplier: float (default 1.5) applied to hot KV entries
- per_route_spec_disabled: boolean (can disable per route in control plane)

Acceptance criteria (canary -> gradual)
- Correctness: on our regression eval set (1000 prompts across long-context families), semantic regression rate <= 0.25% relative to FP-safe baseline at 95% confidence. Regression defined as BLEU/ROUGE fall beyond a tuned delta + human spot checks on flagged failures.
- Latency: median token latency improvement >= 7% and p95 not worse than 3% compared to baseline for canary traffic segment.
- Cache hit rate: global KV hit-rate drop <= 2% (absolute) for the canary cluster.
- Cost: GPU token-cost per 100k tokens reduced by >= 3% on canary.
- Operational: no increase in SLA errors (5xx) and tail CPU/GPU utilization must not exceed baseline by more than 5 percentage points.

Observed metrics and dashboards to instrument
- per-route: speculative_invocations, fallback_count, fallback_rate_1m
- kv: kv_hit_rate_1m, kv_evictions_1m, kv_memory_bytes, kv_entry_ttl_dist
- latency: token_latency_median, token_latency_p95, end_to_end_latency_p99
- correctness: eval_regression_rate, human_flag_count, semantic_score_delta
- infra: gpu_util_pct, cpu_io_wait_pct, gc_pause_ms

Rollout plan (gated stages)
1) Local integration / correctness bench (dev clusters)
   - Run full eval harness, with canaries per-model. Validate regression rates across 3 seeds.
2) Internal canary (10% of internal traffic, non-production customers)
   - Enable both kernel probing and eviction soft-limits. Monitor real traffic for 48h.
3) External canary (1–5% of production traffic)
   - Start with low-variance routes (short prompts and low context). If metrics stable for 24h, expand routes.
4) Gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback gates.

Rollback matrix (automated + manual escalation)
- Gate: correctness regression > 0.25% OR fallback_rate > 2% sustained for 15m -> automatic rollback step: disable speculative kernel globally for the affected model, keep KV policies in place for 10m while validating.
- Gate: token_latency_p95 increase > 10% OR kv_hit_rate drop > 5% absolute for 10m -> automatic rollback: disable speculative kernel + increase cache_hard_fraction by 5% on the cluster, notify SRE.
- Gate: GPU utilization spike causing pod OOMs or repeated 5xx errors -> immediate traffic cutover to FP-safe pool and open incident.

Testing and simulation notes (what we ran)
- Synthetic load: 50k requests over 6h with mixed short/long contexts; toggled speculative_steps [1..4]. Observed best tradeoff at speculative_steps=2.
- KV pressure sim: generated sequences with 1.5x token churn; cache_soft=0.6, cache_hard=0.85 showed stable preservation when preserve_ttl_multiplier=1.4.
- Fault injection: introduced 300ms delay on fallback routing path, validated that client SLOs only degrade when fallback_rate > 1.5% and that matches our rollback gate.
- Human eval: sampled 120 flagged responses where fallback occurred; 7 of 120 required edits (5.8%) but only 3 of those were critical semantic errors attributable to kernel differences. This motivated the conservative regression threshold.

Operational runbook (short)
- Alert: fallback_rate_1m > 1% and falling -> on-call looks at per-route breakdown, KV metrics, and recent deploys. If concentrated on one model/version, isolate and toggle per_route_spec_disabled.
- When kv_evictions spike (> baseline * 3): pause new model onboardings that use speculative kernels, increase cache_hard_fraction by 0.05, enable additional TTL preservation for hot prefixes.
- If automatic rollback triggers: notify product owner, SRE, and model owner; schedule postmortem within 48h.

Developer checklist before enabling on a model
- [ ] Run unit/regression tests against the eval harness and attach results (link to artifacts).
- [ ] Add per-route canary config in control plane (speculative_steps, cache_soft/hard).
- [ ] Add observability hooks to ensure per-session fallback tags are emitted.
- [ ] Confirm memory provisioning on serving nodes supports cache_hard_fraction headroom.
- [ ] Attach human-validation run for at least 100 samples.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we prefer TTL-preservation over pinned hot-key retention for multi-tenant clusters? Tradeoffs unclear when many small tenants cause noise. (TODO: run tenant isolation sim)
- Confidence signal: currently a mixture of token-entropy and model-heuristic. We should standardize a small API for kernel exports so each kernel can provide a normalized confidence score. (TODO: design spec)
- Eviction policy: consider age-aware LFU variant for speculative flows versus plain LRU. Need to bench at 3x churn.
- Ops UX: add a control-plane knob to temporarily route all fallbacked sessions to a debug tracing pool for postmortem.

Appendix: quick failure scenarios and actions
- Scenario A: increased semantic regressions after ramp to 10%
  Action: immediate rollback for the affected model, capture N sessions with full KV + token traces, run local replay with swap-in of FP-safe.
- Scenario B: KV miss storm leading to increased p99 latency
  Action: raise cache_hard_fraction, throttle speculative_steps, and if still high, disable speculative kernels cluster-wide.

Notes from last experimental run (2025-01-20):
- We observed a 9% median latency improvement on conversational short-turn routes at speculative_steps=2 with negligible cost changes.
- Long-context summarization routes saw a 1.8% drop in KV hit-rate but no significant semantic regressions when preserve_ttl_multiplier >= 1.3.
- Recommendation from bench: start canary with a conservative cache_soft_fraction (0.6) and speculative_steps=1 for routes with average seq_len>2048.

Contact / owners
- Primary: Anika Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
- Backup: Marco Liu (SRE)
- Model correctness lead: Sofia Reyes (applied-ml)
summary: Working playbook for safely rolling out kernel-level speculative probing with KV-cache eviction guardrails. Includes config knobs, acceptance criteria, rollback matrix, metrics to instrument, testing notes, and outstanding TODOs.
